title: Inside cx-10: Specs, Components & Design Details

spans.text: cx-10 is the product code for the Wolf Hunt F0-60DB booster, a stamina-type top in Takara Tomy's Beyblade X Custom Line that went on sale in Japan on 1 November 2025 at ¥1,700 including tax. This guide breaks down every stock part, the community part ratings, what the top actually does in battle, the real price in Japan and Hong Kong, and the buying traps (launchers, fakes, Hasbro numbering) that the product listings skip. If you are deciding whether Wolf Hunt earns a slot in your deck, the tables and decision framework below give you the answer in about ten minutes.
Key takeaways
CX-10 is the Japan-market product code for Booster Wolf Hunt F0-60DB, the first stamina-type release in the Beyblade X Custom Line (CX), priced at ¥1,700 with tax and released on 1 November 2025.
The blade splits into three swappable pieces (Wolf Lock Chip, Hunt Main Blade, Free Assist Blade), so a complete CX top has five parts instead of the three in the BX and UX lines.
The stock build is stamina/right-spin: Hunt gives Stamina 30, the Free assist blade adds Defense 25, and the Disc Ball bit tops the chart at Stamina 55 in the community part ratings.
A booster ships without a launcher; you need a separate Beyblade X launcher and stadium before you can battle.
In Hong Kong the official Takara Tomy Asia mall lists it as 戰狼狩獵 at HKD $79.90 suggested retail, while Hasbro's western CX releases use their own separate product numbering.
What is cx-10?

CX-10 is the product code for Booster Wolf Hunt F0-60DB, a stamina-type, right-spin booster in Takara Tomy's Beyblade X Custom Line. It launched in Japan on 1 November 2025 at ¥1,700 tax included, and its blade splits into three swappable pieces for customisation, per
Takara Tomy's official CX-10 page
That single sentence hides three things new buyers trip over, so let us unpack them.
The code vs the name.

"CX-10" is the SKU, not the top's name. The top is called Wolf Hunt, its full stock notation is F0-60DB, and the blade splits into a Wolf Lock Chip, a Hunt Main Blade and a Free Assist Blade. When a friend says "cx-10" and a listing says "Wolf Hunt F0-60DB", they are describing the same product.
Beyblade X parts guide

In Chinese-speaking markets including Hong Kong, Takara Tomy Asia sells the same item as 戰狼狩獵 (meaning "war wolf hunt"), so under that name in local shops and on Carousell you are looking at the identical mould.
The line.

CX stands for Custom Line, the third Beyblade X parts system after the Basic Line (BX) and Unique Line (UX). The Custom Line keeps the Ratchet and Bit but splits the Blade itself into three separate pieces, so a complete CX combo is five parts in total: Lock Chip, Main Blade, Assist Blade, Ratchet and Bit, as the Monkee Mods CX system guide explains. CX-01 Dran Brave opened the line in March 2025, and CX-10 is the tenth numbered Japan-market release.
The format.

"Booster" on the box means the top only. The official product page states plainly that this product requires a separately sold Beyblade X stadium and launcher. Budget for those if this is your first bey.
How the code decodes: F0-60DB
Beyblade X stock notations read as Blade-Ratchet-Bit:
So "F0-60DB" tells you the whole stock combo before you open the box. Once you can read this line, every Beyblade X product code stops being alphabet soup.
Why cx-10 matters: the stamina role and the 3-part blade
The five-part CX stack changes what you can tune

In BX and UX tops, the blade is one fixed unit; its weight and contact profile are locked the moment you pick it. CX breaks that unit apart. The Main Blade is the metal-and-plastic ring that carries most of the mass and does most of the hitting; the Lock Chip and Assist Blade sit around it and are swappable independently, which is where the Custom name comes from. Practically, that means the same Hunt main blade can run defensive, balanced or endurance-tuned profiles depending on which chip and assist blade you pair it with, and parts can move between CX products freely.
Wolf Hunt's job in the current meta
Wolf Hunt is built to deflect hits, preserve spin and grind opponents down through repeated contact. The
Mall of Toys hands-on review
describes a top that weathers aggressive strikes early, then outlasts opponents in marathon exchanges, with the Disc Ball bit keeping it centred and stable even after hard contact. The
Monkee Mods product guide
frames its trade-off honestly: a high-impact hit, a burst or a stadium exit can still end the battle before endurance matters. Stamina wins long fights; it does not win the first three seconds.
battle types explainer

Community threads bear both halves out. The recurring questions on r/BeybladeX about Wolf Hunt are "any good combo?" and "Wolf Hunt or Silver Wolf?", which tells you where the top actually sits: a respected endurance platform and parts donor rather than an instant tournament boss.
Where it fits among the CX releases so far

The Custom Line launched with CX-01 Dran Brave in March 2025, and Japan-market releases have marched through the CX numbering (starters, boosters, random boosters, deck sets) since. Wolf Hunt's job in that sequence is to be the line's first pure stamina flagship, the top you buy when you want to learn endurance play or harvest a free-spinning assist blade and a top-tier bit for your own builds.

What the ratings do and do not tell you

Those numbers describe parts, not results. The same guide is explicit that they are "neither measured win rates nor a promise that the stock combination will beat a particular opponent". Stadium, launch power, opponent match-up and part wear all move the outcome. Treat the table as a map of intent: it tells you what a part is for, and your own repeated testing tells you how it behaves in your hands.
How to test and combo cx-10 properly
You unboxed it, you have a launcher and a stadium. Here is the process the community guides converge on.
Stock first.
Run the F0-60DB build as-is for at least ten launches against the same opponent or the same launch routine. You are calibrating your hands before you judge the top.
Count finishes, not vibes.
Record survival, burst, knockout and extreme-finish results per set. Stamina types win on survival; if you are getting knocked out repeatedly, the problem may be launch angle rather than parts.
Change one part at a time.

Swap the bit first (Disc Ball to Ball or Needle changes the ride height and stability profile dramatically), test ten launches, then consider the ratchet. Changing blade, ratchet and bit simultaneously tells you nothing.
Borrow from the CX pool.
The Hunt main blade pairs with other lock chips and assist blades from any CX release, and the Disc Ball bit drops into any X-line ratchet. This is the whole point of the Custom Line.
CX parts compatibility
Log everything.
Write down each configuration and its results. After three sessions you will have a personal win table that beats any online tier list for your local meta.

Beyblade X manual hub
hosts the current product manuals and safety guidance; it is worth a skim before your first launch, particularly the stadium-safety points about keeping faces and hands clear.
Two combos worth trying first
Endurance benchmark:
keep Hunt + Free but swap the ratchet to a taller 7-60 style unit if you own one; the extra height helps the free blade deflect low hits.
Recoil control:
Wolf lock chip with a heavier defensive assist blade turns the build into a wall that leans on the Disc Ball's self-correction, good practice against the attack-types your friends probably run.

Treat both as starting points for your own table, not netdeck answers. The same CX system guide makes the point: with five-part combos, the combination space is so large that first-hand testing beats borrowed configurations.
How to get started with cx-10
Buy the booster plus the essentials.

CX-10 itself, one Beyblade X launcher and a stadium. In Hong Kong the official Takara Tomy Asia mall carries the full X line including launchers and stadiums, and the official Asia mall listing shows the local suggested retail.
Check the sticker before paying.
Takara Tomy products carry the JP/EU/Asia distribution stickers; fakes often skip the barcode sheet or misspell the notation on the back.
Assemble by the manual.
Lock chip, main blade, assist blade, ratchet, bit, in that order, clicked firmly.
Launch low and smooth.
Stamina tops punish wild launches. Consistency first, power later.
Take it to the local scene.
Once the stock build feels familiar, bring it to a meetup; real opponents teach you more in one evening than a week of solo launches.

Conclusion
Conclusion:

CX-10 is the cleanest answer to "I want a stamina top that also upgrades my parts box": the stock F0-60DB build is a genuine endurance platform, and the Hunt main blade, Free assist blade and Disc Ball bit all outlive the product's own meta relevance inside your other combos. If your collection already leans attack, this is the top that balances it; if you are starting out, buy it together with a launcher and stadium and learn launch discipline on it. Track your battles as you test, because in Hong Kong's growing Beyblade X scene, every confirmed match sharpens both your build choices and your ranking. That is exactly what the
BeyHK
app is for: log the match, have your opponent confirm it, and let the local ladder show whether Wolf Hunt's endurance pays off in your hands.

summary.text: Is Wolf Hunt actually good, or just hype?

spans.text: It is a genuinely strong stamina platform with a real weakness: fast kills. The stock build excels at long, grinding exchanges and recovers from hits that would wobble other tops out, but a clean attack hit or a burst ends the fight early. Community discussion has cooled from launch hype, which usually means the top has settled into its true role: parts donor and endurance specialist rather than everything-beater.

summary.text: What is the difference between cx-10 and the Silver Wolf bey?

spans.text: Silver Wolf is a different product line entry (and a different lock chip); Wolf Hunt is the CX-10 booster with the Hunt main blade and Free assist blade. They share the wolf theme and the anime character link, which is exactly why the comparison comes up so often in community threads. They play differently: check the stock notation of each before assuming they are interchangeable.

summary.text: Can I mix cx-10 parts with BX and UX tops?

spans.text: The ratchet and bit: yes, all X-line ratchets and bits are cross-compatible. The blade parts: only within the Custom Line. The three-piece blade stack (lock chip, main blade, assist blade) exists only on CX tops, so Hunt, Free and Wolf cannot mount on a BX or UX blade unit. That is the main reason CX buyers end up wanting at least one more CX release.

summary.text: Is there a fake cx-10 risk when buying in Hong Kong?

spans.text: Counterfeit beyblades circulate on marketplaces and second-hand platforms everywhere, Hong Kong included. Buy from the official Takara Tomy Asia mall or an authorised retailer, check the product sticker and notation printing, and be sceptical of prices far below the official suggested retail. The mould quality on fakes genuinely changes how the top battles, so the cheap listing usually is not a bargain.

summary.text: What should I buy with cx-10 for a first setup?

spans.text: A launcher and a stadium, in that order; the booster is unplayable without them. If a friend already owns a stadium, a shared one works for casual testing. Add a second top with a different battle type (any cheap attack-type booster) so you can run real match-ups instead of mirror matches, then bring both to your local scene and start logging results.
